items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: And then you have swing and then it worked into bebop and then it worked into, I don’t know, Miles Davis and then Coltrane and Thelonious Monk

ctx.x: You said something interesting I thought about bluegrass music is that it’s not all that old, and it’s not old enough to have rules.

Yeah well I mean jazz is the same thing. Each era of jazz you could say wow that’s not that old either. But they move through. The nice thing about jazz is that it moved through. You have like that Louis Armstrong thing but then it moved to another place. And then you have swing and then it worked into bebop and then it worked into, I don’t know, Miles Davis and then Coltrane and Thelonious Monk and then it moved into “Bitches Brew” and the fusion era started, and then you’ve got neotraditionalism coming back and…
Jazz has changed so much so fast.
